title: Boss: the notification service that ate its memory
summary: A bounded mail queue that says no in time, a partner limit that never leaks a slot, and an import that stops at the first failure.

steps.title: The ticket
body: **INC-5120: notifications pod OOMKilled three times during the partner outage.**
$ kubectl describe pod notify-7d9f -n prod | grep -A2 'Last State'
Last State:  Terminated   Reason: OOMKilled   Exit Code: 137
warn: Partner[0] 429 Too Many Requests (in flight: 61)
warn: Partner[0] in flight: 5 of 5 ... in flight: 5 of 5 ... (all requests now waiting)
fail: Import[0] file 2 of 400 failed: bad header; import kept going and wrote 398 partial files
Three coordination bugs: an unbounded queue, a concurrency limit that leaks slots on errors, and a batch that ignores its first

steps.title: 1. A queue that says no in time
prompt: Write a class **`MailQueue(int capacity)`** backed by a **bounded** `Channel<string>` (full mode `Wait`):
- **`ValueTask<bool> TryEnqueueAsync(string mail, TimeSpan wait, CancellationToken ct)`**: write the mail, waiting at most `wait`
for room; return `true` if it was queued, `false` if the queue stayed full (the endpoint then answers 503). If `ct` is cancelled,
- **`IAsyncEnumerable<string> ReadAllAsync(CancellationToken ct)`** for the sender, and **`void Complete()`**.
Write the channel types with their namespace: `System.Threading.Channels.Channel`, `...BoundedChannelOptions`,
starter: public async ValueTask<bool> TryEnqueueAsync(string mail, TimeSpan wait, CancellationToken ct)
solution: public async ValueTask<bool> TryEnqueueAsync(string mail, TimeSpan wait, CancellationToken ct)
template: Dojo.Check("The first mail is queued", await dojoQ.TryEnqueueAsync("a", TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(30), CancellationToken.None), "");
Dojo.Check("The second mail is queued", await dojoQ.TryEnqueueAsync("b", TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(30), CancellationToken.None), "");
Dojo.Check("A third mail is refused once the queue stays full", !await dojoQ.TryEnqueueAsync("x", TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(30), CancellationToken.None),
"The queue accepted a third mail with capacity 2: it is not bounded (or ignores the wait).");
Dojo.Eq("The sender reads the oldest mail first", "a", dojoReader.Current);
Dojo.Check("After a read there is room again", await dojoQ.TryEnqueueAsync("c", TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2), CancellationToken.None), "");
await Dojo.ThrowsAsync<OperationCanceledException>("A cancelled caller gets OperationCanceledException, not false",
Dojo.Eq("After Complete, the sender drains what is left", new List<string> { "b", "c" }, dojoRest);
hints: Create the channel with `Channel.CreateBounded<string>(new BoundedChannelOptions(capacity) { FullMode = BoundedChannelFullMode.Wait })`.
For the wait: a linked `CancellationTokenSource` with `CancelAfter(wait)`, passed to `WriteAsync`; catch `OperationCanceledException` `when (!ct.IsCancellationRequested)` and return false.

steps.title: 2. A partner limit that never leaks
prompt: The partner allows 5 calls in flight from us. `PartnerClient` enforces that with a `SemaphoreSlim`, but releases the slot only after a
**successful** call: every failed call leaks a slot, and after five failures every request waits forever.
Fix **`PartnerClient(Func<string, CancellationToken, Task<string>> call, int maxInFlight)`** and its
**`Task<string> GetAsync(string id, CancellationToken ct)`** so that a slot is always given back, failures still reach the caller,
and at most `maxInFlight` calls run at once across **all** callers.
starter: class PartnerClient(Func<string, CancellationToken, Task<string>> call, int maxInFlight)
public async Task<string> GetAsync(string id, CancellationToken ct)
solution: class PartnerClient(Func<string, CancellationToken, Task<string>> call, int maxInFlight)
public async Task<string> GetAsync(string id, CancellationToken ct)
template: foreach (var dojoId in new[] { "p1", "p2", "p3", "p4" }) dojoGates[dojoId] = new TaskCompletionSource<string>(TaskCreationOptions.RunContinuationsAsynchronously);
async Task<string> DojoCall(string id, CancellationToken ct)
Dojo.Eq("Only two calls run at once", 2, Volatile.Read(ref dojoInFlight));
await Dojo.ThrowsAsync<InvalidOperationException>("A failed call reaches the caller", () => dojoTasks[0]);
var dojoAfter = await Task.WhenAny(Task.WhenAll(dojoTasks[2], dojoTasks[3]), Task.Delay(2000));
Dojo.Check("After two failures, waiting calls still get a slot", dojoTasks[2].IsCompleted && dojoTasks[3].IsCompleted,
"Calls 3 and 4 never started: the failed calls kept their slots. Release in finally.");
if (dojoTasks[3].IsCompletedSuccessfully) Dojo.Eq("Later calls return their results", "ok-4", await dojoTasks[3]);
Dojo.Eq("Never more than two at once", 2, dojoPeak);
hints: The release must run whether the call succeeds or throws.
`await _slots.WaitAsync(ct); try { return await call(id, ct); } finally { _slots.Release(); }`

steps.title: 3. Stop at the first failure
prompt: Write **`static async Task ImportAsync(IReadOnlyList<string> files, Func<string, CancellationToken, Task> import, int maxParallel, CancellationToken ct)`**
- pass each import the loop's token, so that **the first failure cancels the imports still running** and no new ones start;
- the failure's exception comes out of `ImportAsync`.
starter: static async Task ImportAsync(IReadOnlyList<string> files, Func<string, CancellationToken, Task> import, int maxParallel, CancellationToken ct)
solution: static async Task ImportAsync(IReadOnlyList<string> files, Func<string, CancellationToken, Task> import, int maxParallel, CancellationToken ct)
var options = new ParallelOptions { MaxDegreeOfParallelism = maxParallel, CancellationToken = ct };
await Parallel.ForEachAsync(files, options, async (file, token) => await import(file, token));
template: async Task DojoImport(string file, CancellationToken ct)
lock (dojoLock) { dojoStarted++; dojoInFlight++; dojoPeak = Math.Max(dojoPeak, dojoInFlight); if (dojoInFlight == 2) dojoTwoRunning.TrySetResult(); }
if (file == "file-1") { await dojoTwoRunning.Task; throw new InvalidDataException("bad header"); }
var dojoEnded = await Task.WhenAny(dojoRun, Task.Delay(3000)) == dojoRun;
Dojo.Check("The import ends after the first failure", dojoEnded, "It was still running 3 seconds later: the other imports were not cancelled.");
if (dojoEnded) await Dojo.ThrowsAsync<InvalidDataException>("The failure comes out of ImportAsync", () => dojoRun);
Dojo.Check("The import still running was cancelled", dojoCancelled >= 1, "Pass the loop's token to import(file, token).");
Dojo.Check("No more than 2 ran at once", dojoPeak <= 2, $"Peak was {dojoPeak}.");
Dojo.Check("Most files were never started", dojoStarted <= 3, $"{dojoStarted} of 10 were started.");
hints: `await Parallel.ForEachAsync(files, options, async (file, token) => await import(file, token));`: use the `token` the loop gives you, not `ct`.
explain: `Parallel.ForEachAsync` cancels the token it passes to bodies as soon as one throws, stops handing out new items, waits for the
